target.title: Tool outputs sometimes render as image attachments and become unreadable to the agent
target.body:
## Summary

In long-running / ANSI-heavy tool workflows, tool results can collapse into an image attachment placeholder like `(see attached image)` from the agent's perspective. Once that happens, the agent cannot read the original stdout/stderr text, even though that text is often the evidence needed to decide whether a test/build/cron check passed.

This looks like a tool-result rendering / transcript-sanitization fallback leaking into the model-visible tool result without a machine-readable text fallback.

## Repro observed

1. In a long session, run a verbose command with lots of ANSI/test-runner output, e.g. a full test suite.
2. The tool output becomes visible to the agent only as `(see attached image)`.
3. After that, even smaller tool calls such as short `grep`, `read`, or summarized status outputs may also return only `(see attached image)` in the agent-visible result.
4. The agent has to work around it by redirecting output to files, using `NO_COLOR=1`, `tail`/`awk`, and exit-code-only gates.

## Expected behavior

Tool results should always preserve a model-readable text fallback:

- raw stdout/stderr, or
- a bounded/truncated text excerpt, plus a pointer to the full artifact, or
- an explicit `plainText`/`textFallback` field when a UI/media attachment is produced.

If the UI wants to render large output as an image/attachment, that is fine, but the agent should still receive enough text to reason over the result.

## Actual behavior

The agent-visible tool result can become just:

```text
(see attached image)
```

At that point the agent cannot inspect pass/fail counts, errors, file contents, or command output unless it reruns commands with special output-shaping workarounds.

## Impact

This breaks normal agent verification loops:

- test/build/lint output becomes unreadable;
- pass/fail evidence is hidden from the agent;
- subsequent small tool calls may stay affected in the same session;
- the agent may need to spawn fresh sessions or rerun commands purely to recover readable evidence;
- external/irreversible actions become riskier because the verification evidence is obscured.

## Workarounds used

- redirect full logs to files;
- print only short summaries;
- use `NO_COLOR=1` / `TERM=dumb`;
- rely on `set -e` and exit codes;
- avoid long tool stdout in the active conversation.

These are workable but fragile; the platform should keep a text fallback automatically.

## Environment

Observed on OpenClaw `2026.6.11` during a Telegram-sourced main agent session using exec/read tool calls.
